title: Adoption by any product
statement: A product adopts Lathe in its own repo, adds the kinds it needs without forking the schema, and keeps using it as its spec grows large.
measure: The product repos outside this one whose `lathe check` runs on the published package with its schema unchanged, counted from the installs the Owner knows of; and, for specs about ten times Lathe's own size, whether an edit still shows within the Platform performance budgets.
target: At least two such product repos, none with a forked schema, within six months of the first published release; at ten times Lathe's size, an edit visible within 500 ms and checks within 4 s.
measured_outside: The Owner counts the product repos outside this one whose `lathe check` runs on the published package, from the installs they know of, and looks in each for a schema of its own; no test or record in this repo can see another repo. The size part is measured in this repo by the performance suite on the large synthetic product.

title: Right first time
statement: An Agent that builds from the spec gets the change right the first time: what it builds matches the use cases, rules and tests it was given, so the change merges without being sent back.
measure: The share of an Agent's changes built from the spec that merge into main without rework (no send-back for a missed requirement or rule, and no fix-up commit on the same work before it merges), counted each month from the merges the Owner reviews. Second, hand-written accidental code: the share of Lathe's accidental records (its technical records and engineering standards) that are hand-written fills of a pattern's slot or that nothing accounts for, read from Lathe's own check, which lists each domain's accidental debt and warns of each accidental record nothing accounts for.
target: At least 80% within three months of the first published release, and 90% within a year. Hand-written accidental code shrinks: under 20% of Lathe's accidental records are fills or unaccounted for by 2027-06-30.
measured_outside: The Owner tallies each month, from the branches they review and merge, which of an Agent's changes merged as first handed in and which were sent back or needed a fix-up for something the spec said; no test in this repo sees the review.

title: Status from the spec
statement: The Owner learns what is built, proved or still missing from the spec itself, without asking an Agent.
measure: The status questions the Owner still has to ask an Agent each week (what is done, what is tested, what is left) because the spec and its coverage could not answer them, and the coverage claims (designed, built or proved) the Owner finds false on review.
target: At most one such question a week, and no coverage claim found false, within three months of the first published release.
measured_outside: The Owner keeps a weekly tally of the status questions they ask Agents that the spec could not answer, and, for each branch they review, of the records coverage calls designed, built or proved whose claim the code or tests show false (built with nothing implementing it, proved by a test that does not prove it); `lathe check` prints the coverage they compare.

title: Fewer regressions on main
statement: Mistakes a requirement or rule would have caught are caught before they merge, not found later on main.
measure: Defects found on main after a merge that a requirement, rule or test written in the spec would have caught, counted per month.
target: At most one a month, within six months of the first published release.
measured_outside: The Owner records each defect found on main after a merge and judges whether a requirement, rule or test in the spec would have caught it, counting them each month from the fixes they merge.

title: Quick idea to proof
statement: A new piece of behavior goes from written down to built and proved quickly, because the spec tells the Agent exactly what to build and test.
measure: The median days from the commit that first adds a use case to the commit in which its flow test and every one of its use case tests are automated and their files name their IDs, over the use cases added each month.
target: A median under two days, within six months of the first published release.
measured_outside: The Owner takes both dates from git for each use case added in the month: the commit that first adds it, and the first commit on main in which its flow test and every use case test under it are automated and their files name their IDs (Lathe records no test run, so this is the closest proof the history holds); and works out the median each month.

title: Newcomers find their way
statement: A new Agent or Reader, meeting a product for the first time, finds the code and tests behind a requirement quickly from the spec and the app, and a Reader on a phone finds a record and reads it as readily as at a desk.
measure: The time a new Agent or Reader takes to find the code and the tests behind a requirement they are given, timed in a short trial on a product they have not seen. Second, on a phone: the time a Reader takes, from opening the app on a phone, to find a named record and read its statement, timed in the same kind of trial.
target: Under five minutes, median over the trials, within three months of the first published release. On a phone, under 30 seconds, median over the trials, by 2027-03-31.
measured_outside: The Owner runs the trial with each new Agent or Reader: names a requirement, times how long it takes them to name its code file and its tests, and keeps the median. For the phone measure the Owner names a record to a Reader holding a phone with the app open, times until they read its statement aloud, and keeps the median.
